advances: Full-dimensional ordinary volume in dimensions d≥3. The theorem uses an actual real center and the two shifted caps with a common normal. The Hausdorff estimate is local in an ordinary affine frame.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
**Affine reduction and parameter space.** Under $x'=Ax+a$ and $y'=Ay+a$, with $A$ invertible, the new unit normal is $u'=A^{-T}u/\lVert A^{-T}u\rVert_2$ and the new shift is $s'=s/\lVert A^{-T}u\rVert_2$. This maps both halfspaces onto the corresponding new pair and is a bijection of the parameter spaces. All the volumes scale by $|\det A|$. Thus $p_K$ and $P$ are affine invariant with the centers transported, and we first send $S$ onto the standard simplex $T$.

Choose $R>0$ depending only on $d$ with $T\subset R B_2^d$. For centers in $T$, shifts $s\ge2R$ give paired average $1/2$, also attained at $s=2R$, since any supporting hyperplane has zero volume. All minima can therefore be taken on $Q=\mathbb S^{d-1}\times[0,2R]$. The two cap volumes are jointly continuous in $(y,u,s)$ by dominated convergence off the two limiting hyperplanes. Compactness gives a minimum on $Q$, continuity in $y\in T$, and attainment of $P(K)$ on $K$.

**Canonical neighborhoods.** Put $b=1/m$ and $u_i=\nabla\lambda_i/\lVert\nabla\lambda_i\rVert_2$. At $g$, every pair with $s>0$ has average strictly greater than $\Gamma$ by fact 37a5fc541beb1708, applied to the full-dimensional simplex and its centroid. At $s=0$ the paired average is the ordinary cap fraction. Fact 700febf4b7a92759 applies since $g$ has all barycentric coordinates $1/m<1/d$. Its depth formula gives $\Gamma$, and its minimizing edge intercepts have fraction $d/m$ on each edge from the included vertex. Thus the only equality margins are proportional to $\lambda_i-b$ with the indicated orientation. The minimizing pairs in $Q$ are precisely $(u_i,0)$.

Choose pairwise disjoint relative open neighborhoods $U_i\subset Q$ of these parameters with nonempty complement. Shrink them and choose $\chi>0$ so that for $y\in T$ with $\max_j|\lambda_j(y)-b|\le\chi$ and $(u,s)\in U_i$, both margins
$$
\lVert\nabla\lambda_i\rVert_2\,[u\cdot(x-y)-s],\qquad
\lVert\nabla\lambda_i\rVert_2\,[u\cdot(x-y)+s]
$$
are within $\eta$ of $\lambda_i(x)-b$ uniformly on $T$. This follows from continuity on the compact simplex and equality of the margins at $(g,u_i,0)$. Since $\eta<b\le1-b$, both caps strictly contain $v_i$ and strictly exclude all other vertices. On the compact complement $Q\setminus\bigcup_i U_i$, the minimum simplex paired fraction at $g$ is $\Gamma+\rho_0$ for some $\rho_0>0$. By joint continuity and compactness, after shrinking $\chi$ the simplex fraction on that complement is at least $\Gamma+\rho_0/2$ for every such $y$. These choices use only $T$ and $d$.

**One actual center.** Put $B=2^d/\Gamma$ and choose
$$
\tau_*=\min\{\Gamma/2,\ m\Gamma\chi,\ \rho_0/4,\ \Gamma c/(4B)\},\qquad
\delta_d=\min\{1/4,\ c/(4d),\ \tau_*/d\}.
$$
The inner homothet gives $\tau\le 1-(1-\delta)^d\le d\delta\le\tau_*$. The relative simplex hypotheses of fact c99394a395ea2399 hold for its stated loss bounds, since $K$ has the required facet-centroid contacts and $\delta\le\min\{1/2,c/(4d)\}$. Hence $\bar L\le\Gamma(1-c/2)\tau$. The arbitrary-threshold bound of fact 275b3b7cccde92d4 applies to each nearby margin because $\eta\le(1-\delta)/(4m)$ and $8m\eta(1-\delta)^{-d-1}\le8m\eta\,2^{d+1}$. The lost fraction is also at most $\tau$, so each shifted cap loses at most $L_i$ relative to $|S|$.

Set $\Delta_i=(\bar L-L_i)/(m\Gamma)$ and use the center with $\lambda_i(y)=b+\Delta_i$. These coordinates sum to one, with $|\Delta_i|\le\tau/(m\Gamma)$ since $0\le L_i,\bar L\le\tau$. Each coordinate is at least $b/2>\delta/m$, so $y$ is interior to the inner homothet and to $K$. Also $\max_i|\Delta_i|\le\chi$.

**Both cap regimes.** In $U_i$ put $h=u\cdot(v_i-y)$. The two simplex caps have edge intercept fractions $(h\mp s)/[u\cdot(v_i-v_j)]$ on the edges toward $v_j$, $j\ne i$. Their numerators and denominators are positive, and each fraction is less than one by strict isolation. Hence their fractions of $|S|$ are $A_u(h-s)^d$ and $A_u(h+s)^d$ for the same $A_u=\prod_{j\ne i}[u\cdot(v_i-v_j)]^{-1}$. Their average is at least $A_uh^d$ by convexity of the $d$th power on nonnegative arguments. The latter is the through-$y$ simplex cap fraction. Indeed, the through-$y$ cap also isolates $v_i$. For its reciprocal intercepts $a_j=u\cdot(v_i-v_j)/h$ one has $\sum_{j\ne i}a_j\lambda_j(y)=1$ by the barycentric representation of $y$. AM–GM gives
$$
A_uh^d=\prod_{j\ne i}a_j^{-1}\ge d^d\prod_{j\ne i}\lambda_j(y)
\ge \Gamma-m\Gamma\Delta_i-B\tau^2 .
$$
For the last inequality expand $\Gamma\prod_{j\ne i}(1+m\Delta_j)$. The linear term is $-m\Gamma\Delta_i$, and all terms of degree at least two have combined absolute value at most $\Gamma 2^d(\tau/\Gamma)^2=B\tau^2$ since $\tau/\Gamma\le1$.

Each of the two lost fractions is at most $L_i$, so their average is at most $L_i$. This gives, for the paired cap volume of $K$ measured relative to $|S|$, the lower bound
$$
\Gamma-m\Gamma\Delta_i-B\tau^2-L_i
=\Gamma-\bar L-B\tau^2
\ge\Gamma-\Gamma(1-c/2)\tau-B\tau^2 .
$$
On $Q\setminus\bigcup_i U_i$, the simplex fraction is at least $\Gamma+\rho_0/2$ and the mean lost fraction is at most $\tau\le\rho_0/4$, giving a bound greater than $\Gamma$. Larger shifts give the same fraction as the endpoint $s=2R$. After dividing the lower bound by $1-\tau$, we obtain
$$
p_K(y)-\Gamma\ge\frac{\Gamma c\,\tau/2-B\tau^2}{1-\tau}\ge \frac{\Gamma c}{4}\tau ,
$$
since $\tau\le\Gamma c/(4B)$. The estimates include $\tau=0$, when $y=g$.

**Hausdorff consequence.** Fact a839bfd22b7f11a2 gives a minimum-volume enclosing simplex. Work in the reference frame $T$ and choose any minimizing $S$. Let $\varepsilon=d_{H,\infty}(K,T)\le\varepsilon_d$. Because $\varepsilon\le1/[64(d+1)^3]$, fact e823c82617a0bc70 in dimension $d$ gives every facet-centroid contact and labels the vertices within $8d^3\varepsilon\le L\varepsilon$ of the corresponding vertices of $T$. Consequently $d_{H,\infty}(S,T)\le L\varepsilon$ and $\lVert g_S-g_T\rVert_\infty\le L\varepsilon$. The infinity ball of radius $1/[d(d+1)]$ about $g_T=(1/m,\ldots,1/m)$ lies in $T$, as each coordinate stays nonnegative and their sum stays at most one. Writing $h_C$ for the support function of a convex body $C$, for any $u$ we have
$$
\begin{aligned}
h_{(1-\delta_d)S+\delta_d g_S}(u)
&=(1-\delta_d)h_S(u)+\delta_d u\cdot g_S\\
&\le h_T(u)-\frac{\delta_d}{d(d+1)}\lVert u\rVert_1+L\varepsilon\lVert u\rVert_1\\
&\le h_T(u)-\varepsilon\lVert u\rVert_1\le h_K(u).
\end{aligned}
$$
The second inequality uses the defining bound on $\varepsilon_d$. Support-function comparison gives $(1-\delta_d)S+\delta_d g_S\subseteq K\subseteq S$. The relative part gives the asserted bound at an actual point, hence for $P(K)$. The affine change of variables preserves all minimizing enclosures and their volume ratios.
statement:
For a full-dimensional convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^d$, write $\Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d$. For $y\in K$, a unit vector $u$ and $s\ge0$, put $H_\pm(y,u,s)=\{x:u\cdot(x-y)\ge\pm s\}$ and
$$
p_K(y)=\min_{\lVert u\rVert_2=1,\ s\ge0}\frac{|K\cap H_+(y,u,s)|+|K\cap H_-(y,u,s)|}{2|K|},\qquad
P(K)=\max_{y\in K}p_K(y).
$$
Here $|\cdot|$ is ordinary $d$-dimensional volume.

Let $d\ge3$, $m=d+1$, and $c=(1-d^{1-d})/[(d-1)^2m]$. There exists $\delta_d>0$ depending only on $d$ such that for every full-dimensional simplex $S$ with centroid $g$, and every convex body $K$ with
$$
g+(1-\delta)(S-g)\subseteq K\subseteq S,\qquad 0\le\delta\le\delta_d,
$$
whose intersection with each facet of $S$ contains that facet's centroid, there is one $y\in\operatorname{int}K$ such that
$$
p_K(y)-\Gamma\ \ge\ \frac{\Gamma c}{4}\left(1-\frac{|K|}{|S|}\right).
$$
With $\tau=1-|K|/|S|$ and barycentric functions $\lambda_i$ of $S$, one may take $\lambda_i(y)=1/m+(\bar L-L_i)/(m\Gamma)$, where
$$
\eta=\min\left\{\frac1{8m},\frac{\Gamma c}{4\cdot 8m\cdot 2^{d+1}}\right\},\quad
R_i=\frac{|(S\setminus K)\cap\{\lambda_i\ge1/m\}|}{|S|},\quad
L_i=\min\{\tau,R_i+8m\eta\,2^{d+1}\tau\},\quad \bar L=\frac1m\sum_i L_i.
$$

In the ordinary affine frame of a reference simplex, let $T=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,\ldots,e_d)$, $L=8(d+1)^3$, and
$$
\varepsilon_d=\min\left\{\frac1{64(d+1)^3},\ \frac{\delta_d}{d(d+1)(L+1)}\right\}.
$$
If the Hausdorff distance in the infinity norm satisfies $d_{H,\infty}(K,T)\le\varepsilon_d$, a minimum-volume enclosing simplex exists, and every such simplex $S$ satisfies $P(K)-\Gamma\ge(\Gamma c/4)(1-|K|/|S|)$. The claim applies in any ordinary affine image of this frame.
title: Local simplex stability for paired halfspace depth
